name: Zoroaster (Zarathustra)
summary: Ancient Iranian spiritual leader and prophet who founded Zoroastrianism, articulating the cosmic struggle between good (Asha) and evil (Druj) under Ahura Mazda.

name: King Solomon
summary: Third king of Israel, celebrated for legendary wisdom, immense wealth, building the First Temple in Jerusalem, and biblical writings including Proverbs and Ecclesiastes.

name: Elijah
summary: Hebrew prophet who defended the worship of Yahweh against the Phoenician cult of Baal, triumphing at Mount Carmel and taken to heaven in a whirlwind by a chariot of fire.

name: Homer
summary: Legendary ancient Greek epic poet traditionally credited with composing the 'Iliad' and the 'Odyssey', the foundational literary masterpieces of Western culture.

name: Isaiah
summary: Major Hebrew prophet of the Kingdom of Judah renowned for poetic majesty, profound moral vision, and prophetic passages celebrating peace and messianic redemption.

name: Nebuchadnezzar II
summary: King of the Neo-Babylonian Empire who reconstructed Babylon as an imperial jewel, built the Ishtar Gate and legendary Hanging Gardens, and captured Jerusalem initiating the Babylonian Exile.

name: Daniel
summary: Hebrew prophet and court official in Babylon whose unwavering faith delivered him from the lions' den, and whose visions provide foundational apocalyptic prophecy in biblical literature.

name: Cyrus the Great
summary: Founder of the Achaemenid Persian Empire whose governance pioneered cultural tolerance, local autonomy, and an early charter of human rights via the Cyrus Cylinder.

name: Mahavira
summary: Twenty-fourth and last Tirthankara of Jainism who revitalized Jain philosophy, establishing the supreme ethic of non-violence (Ahimsa) and ascetic self-discipline.

name: Gautama Buddha
summary: Ancient Indian ascetic, sage, and philosopher on whose teachings Buddhism was founded, expounding the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path to liberation from suffering.

name: Darius the Great
summary: Third monarch of the Persian Achaemenid Empire who centralized empire governance through twenty satrapies, standard coinage (darics), the Royal Road, and the palaces of Persepolis.

name: Leonidas I
summary: Spartan king of the Agiad line who led the heroic stand of 300 Spartans and allied Greeks at the Battle of Thermopylae in 480 BC against the massive Persian invasion.

name: Esther
summary: Jewish queen of Persian King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) who risked her life to thwart Haman's plot to annihilate the Jewish people, commemorated in the holiday of Purim.

name: Pericles
summary: Prominent Athenian statesman and general who presided over Athens's Golden Age, championing direct democracy and commissioning the Parthenon on the Acropolis.

name: Herodotus
summary: Ancient Greek writer from Halicarnassus acclaimed as the 'Father of History', who authored The Histories chronicling the origins and events of the Greco-Persian Wars.

name: Thucydides
summary: Athenian general and historian known as the father of scientific history and political realism for his impartial, evidence-based History of the Peloponnesian War.

name: Hippocrates
summary: Ancient Greek physician of the Island of Kos revered as the 'Father of Medicine', who separated medicine from superstition, established clinical ethics, and inspired the Hippocratic Oath.

name: Chanakya (Kautilya)
summary: Ancient Indian philosopher, jurist, and prime minister who engineered the rise of the Maurya Empire under Chandragupta Maurya and authored the foundational treatise Arthashastra.

name: Zhuangzi
summary: Influential Chinese Taoist philosopher of the Warring States period celebrated for his paradoxical parables, philosophical skepticism, and the butterfly dream paradox.

name: Alexander the Great
summary: King of Macedonia and undefeated military strategist who conquered the Persian Empire, creating an empire spanning three continents and ushering in the Hellenistic era.

name: Ashoka the Great
summary: Third Emperor of the Maurya Empire of India who, moved by remorse over the bloodshed of the Kalinga War, embraced Buddhism and governed through non-violence and moral edicts.

name: Archimedes
summary: Ancient Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer, and astronomer of Syracuse, regarded as the greatest scientist of antiquity (buoyancy principle, levers, pi calculation).

name: Han Feizi
summary: Warring States Chinese philosopher who synthesized Chinese Legalism (Fajia), advocating strict codified law, statecraft methods (Shu), and sovereign power (Shi) which guided the Qin Dynasty.

name: Eratosthenes
summary: Greek polymath and chief librarian of the Library of Alexandria who accurately calculated the Earth's circumference using solar shadows, invented the term geography, and created the Sieve of Eratosthenes.

name: Qin Shi Huang
summary: Founder of the Qin dynasty and first emperor of a unified China, who standardized currency, weights, measures, and Chinese script, and commissioned the Terracotta Army and Great Wall.

name: Hannibal Barca
summary: Carthaginian general revered as one of history's greatest military strategists, who led an army with war elephants across the Alps into Italy and crushed Rome at Cannae.

name: Scipio Africanus
summary: Roman general and statesman of the Second Punic War who outmatched Carthaginian armies in Hispania and decisively defeated Hannibal Barca at the Battle of Zama in 202 BC.

name: Sima Qian
summary: Han Dynasty Chinese court official and scholar revered as the 'Grand Historian' (Taishigong), who chose castration over execution to finish the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji).

name: Hillel the Elder
summary: Influential Jewish religious leader, sage, and scholar whose teachings formed the basis of rabbinic Judaism and the Mishnah, celebrated for gentleness and ethical clarity.

name: Julius Caesar
summary: Roman general, statesman, and dictator whose conquests of Gaul and victory in civil war precipitated the fall of the Roman Republic and emergence of the Roman Empire.

name: Virgil
summary: Augustan Roman poet whose twelve-book epic masterpiece The Aeneid created the national myth of Rome's founding by Trojan hero Aeneas, profoundly shaping European literature.

name: Cleopatra VII
summary: Last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, renowned for her brilliant political acumen, multilingual diplomacy, and strategic alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.

name: Caesar Augustus
summary: First Emperor of the Roman Empire (r. 27 BC–14 AD) whose political reorganization transformed the fallen Republic into the Principate, inaugurating two centuries of Pax Romana.

name: Mary (Mother of Jesus)
summary: Mother of Jesus Christ, revered in Christianity as the Virgin Mary (Theotokos / Mother of God), exemplary in her humble obedience, maternal devotion, and faith.

name: Pontius Pilate
summary: Fifth prefect of the Roman province of Judaea who presided over the trial of Jesus of Nazareth and reluctantly ordered his crucifixion.

name: Jesus of Nazareth
summary: First-century Jewish preacher and religious leader whose life, teachings, crucifixion, and resurrection form the central core of Christianity and reshaped world civilization.

name: Simon Peter
summary: First among Jesus's Twelve Apostles, prominent early Christian leader in Jerusalem and Rome, regarded by Catholic tradition as the first Bishop of Rome (Pope).

name: Mary Magdalene
summary: Devoted disciple of Jesus Christ who witnessed the Crucifixion, accompanied his burial, and was the first recorded witness to the Resurrection (Apostola Apostolorum).

name: Judas Iscariot
summary: One of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus infamous for betraying Christ to the Sanhedrin for thirty pieces of silver with a kiss in Gethsemane.

name: Paul the Apostle
summary: Apostle to the Gentiles and foundational theologian of early Christianity whose missionary journeys and Epistles shaped Christian doctrine, ethics, and world history.

name: Caligula
summary: Third Roman Emperor whose brief four-year reign became legendary in Roman historiography for cruelty, extravagance, despotism, and alleged insanity.

name: Nero
summary: Fifth Roman emperor of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, remembered for extravagant theatricality, the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, building the Domus Aurea, and initiating Christian persecution.

name: Trajan
summary: Second of the 'Five Good Emperors', under whose military leadership and civic welfare programs (Alimenta) the Roman Empire reached its maximum territorial extent.

name: Hadrian
summary: Third of the 'Five Good Emperors' of Rome, noted for consolidating imperial frontiers, commissioning Hadrian's Wall across Britain, rebuilding the Pantheon, and patronizing the arts.

name: Nagarjuna
summary: Indian Buddhist philosopher regarded as the founder of the Madhyamaka (Middle Way) school, articulating the doctrine of emptiness (Shunyata) and two truths.

name: Constantine the Great
summary: Roman Emperor who legalized Christianity with the Edict of Milan (313), convened the Council of Nicaea, and founded Constantinople (New Rome) as the imperial capital.

name: Augustine of Hippo
summary: Early Christian theologian, philosopher, and bishop of Hippo Regius whose writings on grace, original sin, time, and the City of God shaped Western philosophy and theology.

name: Hypatia
summary: Hellenistic Neoplatonist philosopher, astronomer, and mathematician in Alexandria, revered for teaching geometry and astronomy to students across the Mediterranean.

name: Kalidasa
summary: Classical Sanskrit author widely regarded as ancient India's greatest poet and dramatist, whose works like Shakuntala capture sublime lyrical beauty and profound psychological depth.

name: Saint Patrick
summary: Romano-British Christian missionary and bishop who converted Ireland to Christianity, celebrated as the primary patron saint of Ireland and author of the Confessio.

name: Pope Leo I
summary: Leo the Great, Church Father and pope who persuaded Attila the Hun to turn back from invading Rome in 452, and whose Tome defined Christ's dual nature at the Council of Chalcedon.

name: Attila the Hun
summary: Ruler of the Huns known to Rome as the 'Scourge of God' (Flagellum Dei), who forged a colossal barbarian empire stretching from Central Asia to the Rhine, challenging both Roman empires.

name: Clovis I
summary: First King of the Franks to unite all Frankish tribes under Merovingian rule, conquering Gaul and converting to Nicene Catholic Christianity at Reims.

name: Bodhidharma
summary: Semi-legendary Buddhist monk who transmitted Chan (Zen) Buddhism from India to China, renowned for sitting in meditation facing a wall at the Shaolin Monastery.

name: Aryabhata
summary: Pioneering Indian mathematician and astronomer of the classical era who computed the approximation of pi, formulated trigonometry (sine tables), and proposed that Earth rotates daily on its axis.

name: Boethius
summary: Roman senator, philosopher, and statesman who wrote The Consolation of Philosophy while imprisoned on false treason charges, transmitting classical Greek philosophy to medieval Europe.

name: Benedict of Nursia
summary: Christian monk regarded as the father of Western monasticism, who founded the monastery of Monte Cassino and wrote the Rule of Saint Benedict embodying balanced devotion.

name: Justinian I (the Great)
summary: Eastern Roman Emperor who codified Roman law into the Corpus Juris Civilis, reconquered Italy and North Africa, and commissioned the architectural wonder Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.

name: Empress Theodora
summary: Byzantine Empress and wife of Justinian I, one of the most influential sovereigns in Roman history, who championed women's legal rights and saved the throne during the Nika Riots.

name: Belisarius
summary: Legendary Byzantine general under Justinian I celebrated as the 'Last of the Romans', whose brilliant tactical genius reconquered Rome, Italy, and North Africa from Vandal and Ostrogoth kingdoms.

name: Pope Gregory I
summary: Gregory the Great, Church Father and pope who instituted liturgical reforms (inspiring Gregorian chant), organized famine relief in Italy, and sent Augustine to convert Anglo-Saxon England.

name: Tang Taizong
summary: Emperor Taizong of Tang (Li Shimin), co-founder and second emperor of China's Tang dynasty, whose enlightened Reign of Zhenguan ushered in a golden age of prosperity and cosmopolitan culture.

name: Brahmagupta
summary: Ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer who wrote the Brahmasphutasiddhanta, presenting the first systematic mathematical treatment of zero and negative numbers.

name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
summary: Cousin and son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad, fourth of the Rashidun caliphs in Sunni Islam, and the first Imam in Shia Islam, celebrated for chivalry, wisdom, and eloquent justice.

name: Xuanzang
summary: Chinese Buddhist monk and scholar whose epic seventeen-year pilgrimage to India along the Silk Road brought hundreds of Sanskrit Buddhist texts back to China, inspiring Journey to the West.

name: Wu Zetian
summary: Sole female sovereign of Imperial China who established the Zhou dynasty, expanded the imperial examinations based on merit, promoted Buddhism, and stabilized the realm.

name: Tariq ibn Ziyad
summary: Berber general of the Umayyad Caliphate who launched the Islamic conquest of the Iberian Peninsula in 711, landing at the Rock of Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq, named after him).

name: Charles Martel
summary: Frankish statesman and military commander known as 'The Hammer' (Martel), who halted the Umayyad expansion into northwestern Europe at the pivotal Battle of Tours (Poitiers) in 732.

name: Li Bai
summary: Tang Dynasty Chinese poet hailed as the 'Poet Immortal' (Shixian), revered for his romantic spontaneity, cosmic imagination, and joyous devotion to moonlit wine and nature.

name: Du Fu
summary: Tang Dynasty Chinese poet revered as the 'Poet Historian' and 'Poet Sage' (Shisheng), whose compassionate, masterfully crafted verses chronicled the devastation of the An Lushan Rebellion.

name: Jabir ibn Hayyan (Geber)
summary: Polymath and alchemist in Kufa hailed as the 'Father of Chemistry', who pioneered systematic laboratory experimentation, distillation, crystallization, and discovered sulfuric and nitric acids.

name: Charlemagne
summary: King of the Franks and first Holy Roman Emperor (crowned by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day 800), who united Western and Central Europe and spearheaded the Carolingian Renaissance.

name: Harun al-Rashid
summary: Fifth Abbasid Caliph whose rule marked the scientific, cultural, and economic zenith of the Islamic Golden Age in Baghdad, immortalized in One Thousand and One Nights.

name: Al-Khwarizmi
summary: Persian polymath in Baghdad's House of Wisdom whose foundational texts introduced systematic algebraic equation solving ('algebra') and Hindu-Arabic numerals ('algorithm').

name: Adi Shankara
summary: Indian philosopher and theologian who consolidated the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta (non-dualism), revitalizing Hindu thought through monumental commentaries and monastic institutions.

name: Rurik
summary: Semi-legendary Varangian (Norse Viking) chieftain invited by East Slavic and Finnic tribes to rule Novgorod, founding the Rurik Dynasty that governed Kievan Rus' and Russia until 1598.

name: Alfred the Great
summary: King of Wessex who successfully defended England against Viking conquest at the Battle of Edington, established the burghal defensive system, and revived English education and law.

name: Al-Farabi
summary: Early Islamic Golden Age philosopher and music theorist known as the 'Second Teacher' (after Aristotle), who integrated Platonic political philosophy with Aristotelian logic.

name: Olga of Kiev
summary: Regent of Kievan Rus' who exacted legendary vengeance upon the Drevlians for her husband's murder, established the realm's first centralized taxation system, and converted to Christianity.

name: Vladimir the Great
summary: Grand Prince of Kiev who unified Kievan Rus' and officially Christianized the realm in 988 through the mass baptism of Kiev in the Dnieper River, linking Russia to Byzantine civilization.

name: Leif Erikson
summary: Norse explorer from Iceland believed to be the first known European to set foot on continental North America ('Vinland', modern Newfoundland at L'Anse aux Meadows).

name: Murasaki Shikibu
summary: Heian-era Japanese noblewoman, poet, and court lady who wrote The Tale of Genji, widely recognized as the world's first complete psychological novel.

name: Al-Biruni
summary: Persian polymath regarded as the 'Father of Indology' and 'Father of Geodesy', who calculated the Earth's radius with remarkable precision and authored monumental works on astronomy and cultures.

name: Pope Gregory VII
summary: Hildebrand of Sovana, reformer pope who spearheaded the Gregorian Reforms, asserted papal primacy against secular monarchs, and clashed with Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV in the Investiture Controversy.

name: William the Conqueror
summary: Duke of Normandy who conquered England in 1066 at the Battle of Hastings, crowned King of England, and commissioned the monumental Domesday Book census.

name: Shen Kuo
summary: Song Dynasty Chinese polymath, statesman, and scientist who first described the magnetic compass needle for navigation, movable type printing, and geological sedimentation.

name: Anselm of Canterbury
summary: Italian-born Benedictine monk, philosopher, and Archbishop of Canterbury hailed as the founder of Scholasticism, renowned for the ontological argument for the existence of God.

name: Pope Urban II
summary: Head of the Catholic Church who launched the First Crusade with his electrifying sermon at the Council of Clermont in 1095, fundamentally reshaping medieval geopolitics.

name: Su Shi (Su Dongpo)
summary: Towering Song Dynasty Chinese poet, essayist, calligrapher, and statesman celebrated for his profound optimism, culinary artistry (Dongpo pork), and sublime ci poetry.

name: Omar Khayyam
summary: Persian polymath, mathematician, astronomer, and poet who solved cubic equations geometrically, reformed the Persian Jalali calendar, and composed the timeless Rubaiyat.

name: Al-Ghazali
summary: Eminent Persian polymath, Islamic jurist, theologian, and mystic whose masterworks reconciled orthodox Sunni Islamic theology with the inner spiritual dimensions of Sufism.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
summary: One of the wealthiest and most powerful women in Western European history, Queen consort of France (Louis VII) and England (Henry II), mother of King Richard the Lionheart and King John.

name: Frederick Barbarossa
summary: Holy Roman Emperor Frederick I of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, renowned for reasserting imperial Corpus Juris Civilis authority, subduing Italian city-states, and leading the Third Crusade.

name: Averroes (Ibn Rushd)
summary: Andalusian polymath, jurist, and philosopher known as 'The Commentator' on Aristotle, whose defense of philosophical reason (Averroism) profoundly ignited the European Renaissance and Scholasticism.

name: Zhu Xi
summary: Song Dynasty Chinese philosopher who synthesized Neo-Confucianism, establishing the Four Books as the core imperial examination curriculum that governed China for centuries.

name: Saladin
summary: First Sultan of Egypt and Syria and founder of the Ayyubid dynasty, revered across both the Islamic and Western worlds for recapturing Jerusalem and displaying chivalric magnanimity.

name: Maimonides
summary: Moses ben Maimon (Rambam), preeminent Sephardic Jewish philosopher, astronomer, and physician whose synthesis of Aristotelian philosophy and Jewish law remains foundational.

name: Minamoto no Yoritomo
summary: Founder and first shogun of the Kamakura shogunate of Japan, who defeated the Taira clan in the Genpei War and initiated seven centuries of samurai warrior rule (Bakufu).

name: Richard the Lionheart
summary: Richard I, King of England and chivalric hero who led the Third Crusade, winning renowned victories at Acre and Arsuf against Saladin while ruling the Angevin Empire.

name: Pope Innocent III
summary: One of the most powerful and influential popes of the Middle Ages, who asserted supreme papal authority over secular monarchs and convened the Fourth Lateran Council.

name: Genghis Khan
summary: Founder and first Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, who united the nomadic tribes of Northeast Asia to forge the largest contiguous land empire in human history.

name: Francis of Assisi
summary: Italian Catholic friar, mystic, and patron saint of ecology who founded the Franciscan Order, renouncing all wealth to practice radical poverty, peace, and brotherhood with nature.

name: Frederick II (Holy Roman Emperor)
summary: Hohenstaufen King of Sicily and Holy Roman Emperor renowned as 'Stupor Mundi' (Wonder of the World) for his polyglot intellect, scientific treatises, and recovery of Jerusalem via diplomacy.

name: Dōgen Zenji
summary: Japanese Buddhist monk, philosopher, and poet who founded the Sōtō school of Zen in Japan, emphasizing 'just sitting' (shikantaza) and the oneness of practice and enlightenment.

name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
summary: Persian polymath, architect, philosopher, and astronomer who founded the Maragheh Observatory and developed the 'Tusi couple', a geometric device that later influenced Copernicus.

name: Rumi (Jalal al-Din Rumi)
summary: 13th-century Persian poet, Islamic scholar, and Sufi mystic whose ecstatic poetry on divine love, unity, and spiritual longing transcended national and religious borders.

name: Saadi Shirazi
summary: Major Persian poet and prose writer celebrated for the lyrical elegance and profound moral humanism of his classics Gulistan (The Rose Garden) and Bustan (The Orchard).

name: Kublai Khan
summary: Grandson of Genghis Khan who founded the Yuan dynasty of China in 1271, ruled as first Mongol Emperor of China, and hosted Venetian traveler Marco Polo at his court in Khanbaliq.

name: Sundiata Keita
summary: Legendary 'Lion King' who founded the Mali Empire in West Africa, defeating King Soumaoro Kanté at the Battle of Kirina and establishing the Kouroukan Fouga oral constitution.

name: Roger Bacon
summary: English Franciscan friar and philosopher known as 'Doctor Mirabilis', an early pioneer of the scientific method and empirical experimentation in optics and nature.

name: Alexander Nevsky
summary: Prince of Novgorod and Grand Prince of Vladimir who repelled Swedish and German invasions at the Battle of the Neva and Battle on the Ice (Lake Peipus), canonized as a saint.

name: Marco Polo
summary: Venetian merchant, explorer, and author whose 24-year journey along the Silk Road to China and court of Kublai Khan introduced Europeans to the culture and technologies of East Asia.

name: Giotto di Bondone
summary: Italian painter and architect from Florence whose naturalistic human emotion and spatial depth initiated the decisive break from Byzantine art, heralding the Renaissance.

name: William Wallace
summary: Scottish knight and national hero who led the Scottish resistance against English rule during the First War of Scottish Independence, triumphant at the Battle of Stirling Bridge.

name: Mansa Musa
summary: Tenth Mansa of the Mali Empire, famed as one of the wealthiest individuals in human history, whose lavish 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca and patronage transformed Timbuktu into a world center of Islamic scholarship.

name: William of Ockham
summary: English Franciscan friar, scholastic philosopher, and theologian whose methodological principle of parsimony ('Occam's Razor') laid foundational groundwork for modern scientific inquiry.

name: Ibn Battuta
summary: Moroccan Islamic scholar and traveler who logged over 73,000 miles across Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, India, Southeast Asia, and China, documented in his 'Rihla'.

name: Petrarch
summary: Italian scholar and poet celebrated as the 'Father of Humanism', whose recovery of classical texts and sonnets to Laura in the Canzoniere sparked the European Renaissance.

name: Giovanni Boccaccio
summary: Italian writer, poet, and humanist whose masterpiece The Decameron established the European prose novella and provided vivid, humorous insight into life during the Black Death.

name: Hafez
summary: Revered Persian lyric poet whose Divan of Hafez represents the pinnacle of Persian ghazal poetry, celebrated across Iran for sublime themes of divine love, ecstasy, and hypocrisy.

name: Zhu Yuanzhang (Hongwu Emperor)
summary: Founding emperor of China's Ming dynasty who rose from peasant poverty and monkhood to lead the Red Turban Rebellion that expelled the Mongol Yuan dynasty and restored Han rule.

name: John Wycliffe
summary: English scholastic philosopher and theologian known as the 'Morning Star of the Reformation', who initiated the first complete translation of the Bible into Middle English.

name: Timur (Tamerlane)
summary: Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire across Central Asia, Persia, and the Levant, remembered both as a devastating military conqueror and patron of the Timurid Renaissance in Samarkand.

name: Geoffrey Chaucer
summary: Author, poet, and courtier acclaimed as the 'Father of English Literature', whose Canterbury Tales legitimized Middle English as a rich literary language equal to French and Latin.

name: Christine de Pizan
summary: Italian-French late medieval author acclaimed as Europe's first professional female writer, whose Book of the City of Ladies defended women against misogynistic slander.

name: Jan Hus
summary: Czech religious reformer and rector of Charles University in Prague whose fiery sermons against Church corruptions launched the Hussite movement; martyred at the Council of Constance.

name: Zheng He
summary: Chinese mariner, explorer, and diplomat who commanded seven monumental treasure fleet voyages for the Ming Dynasty across Southeast Asia, India, the Persian Gulf, and East Africa.

name: Johannes Gutenberg
summary: German inventor and goldsmith who introduced movable type printing to Europe, printing the Gutenberg Bible (1455) and igniting the global Printing Revolution.

name: Vlad the Impaler
summary: Voivode of Wallachia three times whose ferocious defense against Ottoman expansion and notorious punishment of enemies by impalement inspired the Dracula legend.

name: Pope Alexander VI
summary: Rodrigo Borgia, Renaissance Pope infamous for dynastic ambition, diplomatic cunning, and patronizing Pinturicchio, while mediating the Spanish-Portuguese Treaty of Tordesillas.

name: Kabir
summary: 15th-century Indian mystic poet and saint whose earthy, incisive couplets challenged sectarian dogma across Hinduism and Islam, emphasizing direct personal devotion.

name: Pope Julius II
summary: Giuliano della Rovere, the 'Warrior Pope', who consolidated Papal States sovereignty and served as one of the Renaissance's greatest patrons, commissioning Michelangelo and Raphael.

name: Guru Nanak
summary: Founder of Sikhism and first of the ten Sikh Gurus, whose spiritual journeys taught universal equality, oneness of God (Ik Onkar), and honest living.

name: Michelangelo
summary: Italian High Renaissance master sculptor, painter, architect, and poet whose works, including David and the Sistine Chapel ceiling, represent the zenith of Western art.

name: Ferdinand Magellan
summary: Portuguese explorer who organized the Spanish expedition of 1519 to the East Indies, navigating the Strait of Magellan and leading the first expedition to circumnavigate the Earth.

name: Ignatius of Loyola
summary: Spanish Basque knight turned mystic and theologian who founded the Society of Jesus (Jesuits) and authored the transformative Spiritual Exercises.

name: Pope Gregory XIII
summary: Pope famous for introducing the Gregorian Calendar in 1582, correcting inaccuracies of the Julian calendar, and vigorously executing Counter-Reformation educational initiatives.

name: John Calvin
summary: French theologian, pastor, and reformer in Geneva whose systematic theology of Reformed Christianity (Calvinism) emphasized the absolute sovereignty of God and predestination.

name: Andreas Vesalius
summary: Flemish anatomist and physician whose masterpiece De humani corporis fabrica overturned Galen's ancient dogmas through meticulous direct human dissection, founding modern human anatomy.

name: Teresa of Ávila
summary: Spanish mystic, Carmelite nun, and Doctor of the Church who led the Discalced Carmelite reform and penned profound spiritual classics on contemplative prayer.

name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
summary: Japanese daimyo who rose from peasant foot soldier to succeed Oda Nobunaga as the second 'Great Unifier' of Japan, building Osaka Castle and ordering the nationwide sword hunt.

name: Caravaggio
summary: Italian Baroque painter whose radical naturalism and revolutionary chiaroscuro (dramatic light and shadow) reshaped European painting.

name: William Harvey
summary: English physician who was the first to describe completely and in systemic detail the circulation of blood pumped throughout the body by the heart in De Motu Cordis.

name: Artemisia Gentileschi
summary: Italian Baroque painter, the first woman admitted to Florence's Accademia delle Arti del Disegno, celebrated for dramatic, visceral depictions of strong biblical and mythical women.

name: Pierre de Fermat
summary: French lawyer and amateur mathematician who laid foundations for analytic geometry, infinitesimal calculus, probability theory, and formulated Fermat's Last Theorem.

name: Dandara dos Palmares
summary: Afro-Brazilian warrior and military strategist of Quilombo dos Palmares who fought fiercely against Portuguese colonial forces to defend freedom and autonomy for escaped enslaved people.

name: Guru Gobind Singh
summary: Tenth Sikh Guru, spiritual master, warrior, and poet who founded the Khalsa order, introduced the Five Ks, and declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru.

name: Antonio Vivaldi
summary: Venetian Baroque composer and virtuoso violinist known as 'The Red Priest' (Il Prete Rosso), whose Four Seasons violin concertos remain among the most celebrated works in classical music.

name: Baal Shem Tov
summary: Israel ben Eliezer, charismatic mystic and spiritual healer in Eastern Europe who founded Hasidic Judaism, emphasizing joyous prayer, love of fellow humans, and divine immanence.

name: Sepé Tiaraju
summary: Guarani chief and military leader of the Jesuit Reductions who resisted Portuguese and Spanish territorial transfers in the Guaraní War, immortalized by the cry 'Esta terra tem dono!'.

name: James Cook
summary: British navigator, cartographer, and captain in the Royal Navy who made three epic voyages of discovery to the Pacific Ocean, producing the first accurate European maps of New Zealand and eastern Australia.

name: James Watt
summary: Scottish inventor and mechanical engineer whose radical improvements to the Newcomen steam engine with a separate condenser powered the Industrial Revolution.

name: Túpac Amaru II
summary: Quechua kuraka who led the largest anti-colonial indigenous rebellion in 18th-century Spanish South America, declaring the abolition of slavery and indigenous forced labor.

name: Thomas Jefferson
summary: Third President of the United States, principal author of the Declaration of Independence, polymath, and founder of the University of Virginia, who championed liberty and religious freedom.

name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
summary: Austrian composer of the Classical era, widely recognized as one of the greatest musical prodigies in history, composing over 800 works across every musical genre.

name: José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva
summary: Polymath, mineralogist, and 'Patriarch of Independence' who steered Dom Pedro I toward Brazilian sovereignty in 1822 and championed the abolition of slavery.

name: Jane Austen
summary: English novelist whose masterworks of romantic fiction, psychological realism, and brilliant social satire made her one of the most enduring writers in world literature.

name: Maria Quitéria
summary: Brazilian independence heroine who disguised herself as a man ('Soldado Medeiros') to fight in the War of Independence of Bahia (1822–1823), decorated by Emperor Dom Pedro I.

name: Mary Shelley
summary: English novelist who created modern science fiction at age 18 with 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus', an enduring inquiry into scientific ambition, creation, and hubris.

name: Sojourner Truth
summary: African American abolitionist, women's rights activist, and orator born into slavery who delivered the electrifying speech 'Ain't I a Woman?' at the 1851 Akron Convention.

name: Duque de Caxias
summary: Luís Alves de Lima e Silva, Patron of the Brazilian Army, military strategist, and Prime Minister who stabilized the Empire and commanded allied forces in the Paraguayan War.

name: Louis Braille
summary: French educator who, having lost his sight as a child, invented the six-dot embossed tactile reading and writing system (Braille) that revolutionized global literacy for the blind.

name: Frédéric Chopin
summary: Polish composer and virtuoso pianist of the Romantic era, known as the 'poet of the piano' for his expressive nocturnes, ballades, polonaises, and études.

name: Pope Leo XIII
summary: Pope whose intellectual pontificate produced the landmark encyclical Rerum Novarum, establishing modern Catholic social teaching on workers' rights and economic justice.

name: Herman Melville
summary: American novelist, short story writer, and poet of the American Renaissance whose masterpiece 'Moby-Dick' is one of the supreme achievements of world literature.

name: Florence Nightingale
summary: English social reformer, statistician, and founder of modern nursing, acclaimed as 'The Lady with the Lamp' for caring for wounded soldiers during the Crimean War.

name: Anita Garibaldi
summary: Brazilian revolutionary known as the 'Heroine of the Two Worlds', who fought alongside Giuseppe Garibaldi in the Ragamuffin War in southern Brazil and the battles for Italian unification.

name: Harriet Tubman
summary: American abolitionist, Underground Railroad conductor, Union scout, and suffragist who escaped slavery and courageously led dozens of enslaved people to freedom.

name: Gregor Mendel
summary: Austrian Augustinian friar and scientist recognized as the father of modern genetics for his experimental breeding of pea plants, establishing the fundamental laws of genetic inheritance.

name: Geronimo
summary: Prominent Bedonkohe Apache warrior and medicine man who led fierce guerrilla resistance against Mexican and United States military expansion across the American Southwest.

name: Emily Dickinson
summary: Distinctive American poet of Amherst, Massachusetts, whose reclusive life yielded nearly 1,800 intensely compressed, slant-rhymed masterpieces on mortality, faith, and nature.

name: Sitting Bull
summary: Hunkpapa Lakota holy man and tribal chief who united the Sioux tribes of the Great Plains against US military encroachment, defeating Custer at the Battle of the Little Bighorn.

name: Claude Monet
summary: French painter and foundational master of Impressionism, devoted to capturing the fleeting perceptions of light, weather, and color in the natural landscape.

name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
summary: Russian Romantic composer renowned for melodic genius and profound emotional resonance, who composed timeless ballet masterworks Swan Lake, The Nutcracker, and the 1812 Overture.

name: Prudente de Morais
summary: First civilian President of Brazil (1894–1898), who steered the nation from military dictatorship toward civilian constitutional governance through the War of Canudos.

name: Alfred Marshall
summary: English economist who was one of the foremost founders of neoclassical economics, synthesizing supply and demand, marginal utility, and costs of production into a coherent framework.

name: Barão do Rio Branco
summary: José Maria da Silva Paranhos Júnior, Patron of Brazilian Diplomacy, who peacefully defined and secured Brazil's definitive national borders including Acre.

name: Castro Alves
summary: Brazilian poet known as the 'Poet of the Slaves' (O Poeta dos Escravos), whose impassioned Condorist Romantic verse campaigned ardently for the abolition of slavery and republican freedom.

name: Vilfredo Pareto
summary: Italian polymath, engineer, sociologist, and economist who formulated the Pareto efficiency concept in economics and discovered the 80/20 power-law wealth distribution rule (Pareto principle).

name: Gottlob Frege
summary: German mathematician, logician, and philosopher considered one of the founding fathers of modern mathematical logic and analytic philosophy.

name: Rodrigues Alves
summary: Fifth President of Brazil, celebrated for modernizing Rio de Janeiro, expanding port infrastructure, and backing Oswaldo Cruz in eradicating yellow fever and smallpox.

name: Joaquim Nabuco
summary: Diplomat, historian, and preeminent parliamentary champion of Brazilian abolitionism, whose foundational writing exposed slavery as the nation's core moral wound.

name: Rui Barbosa
summary: Jurist, orator, writer, and 'Eagle of The Hague' who co-authored the 1891 Republican Constitution and defended the sovereign equality of nations at the 1907 Hague Conference.

name: Antoni Gaudí
summary: Catalan architect and supreme master of Modernisme, whose bio-morphic, organic architecture culminated in Barcelona's monumental Basílica de la Sagrada Família.

name: Vincent van Gogh
summary: Dutch Post-Impressionist painter whose emotionally expressive brushwork, vivid colors, and dramatic compositions laid the foundations of modern expressionism.

name: Henri Poincaré
summary: French mathematician, theoretical physicist, and philosopher of science hailed as the 'Last Universalist', who founded algebraic topology, chaos theory, and special relativity foundations.

name: Emmeline Pankhurst
summary: British political activist who founded and led the militant suffragette movement (Women's Social and Political Union), instrumental in winning women the right to vote in Britain.

name: Anton Chekhov
summary: Russian playwright and short-story master whose psychological realism, understated poignancy, and dramatic innovation revolutionised modern prose and theatre.

name: David Hilbert
summary: German mathematician recognized as one of the most influential figures of 19th and 20th-century mathematics, formulating Hilbert space, invariant theory, and 23 famous unsolved problems.

name: Henry Ford
summary: American industrialist and founder of Ford Motor Company who developed the moving assembly line for mass production, revolutionizing global manufacturing and the automobile industry.

name: Swami Vivekananda
summary: Indian Hindu monk and chief disciple of Ramakrishna who introduced Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world at the 1893 Chicago Parliament of the World's Religions.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
summary: Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who led the nationwide campaign for Indian independence through nonviolent civil resistance (Satyagraha).

name: Guglielmo Marconi
summary: Italian inventor and electrical engineer who developed the first practical radio wireless telegraphy system, sending the first transatlantic radio signal in 1901; awarded the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Ernest Shackleton
summary: Anglo-Irish polar explorer who led three British expeditions to the Antarctic, legendary for his extraordinary leadership and survival triumph during the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition (Endurance).

name: Lise Meitner
summary: Austrian-Swedish physicist who led the discovery and theoretical explanation of nuclear fission with Otto Hahn and Otto Frisch, unfairly excluded from the 1944 Nobel Prize.

name: Pablo Picasso
summary: Spanish painter and sculptor who co-founded the Cubist movement, invented constructed sculpture, and redefined 20th-century visual art with works like Guernica.

name: Alexander Fleming
summary: Scottish physician and microbiologist who discovered penicillin in 1928, inaugurating the era of modern antibiotics and saving hundreds of millions of lives worldwide.

name: Lima Barreto
summary: Brazilian novelist and journalist whose sharp, socially critical fiction challenged racism, class prejudice, and republican hypocrisy in early 20th-century Rio de Janeiro.

name: Pope John XXIII
summary: Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli, beloved as 'Good Pope John', who convened the transformative Second Vatican Council (Vatican II) to modernize and open the Catholic Church.

name: Emmy Noether
summary: German mathematician described by Einstein as the most significant woman in mathematical history, whose theorem connects continuous symmetries to physical conservation laws.

name: Eleanor Roosevelt
summary: American political figure, diplomat, and activist who served as First Lady, chaired the UN Commission on Human Rights, and spearheaded the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
summary: Self-taught Indian mathematical genius whose intuitive breakthroughs in mathematical analysis, infinite series, continued fractions, and partition theory stunned world mathematics.

name: Charlie Chaplin
summary: English comic actor, filmmaker, and composer who became a worldwide icon through his screen persona 'The Tramp', creating timeless masterworks of silent comedy and social satire.

name: Adolf Hitler
summary: Austrian-born dictator of Nazi Germany whose aggressive militarism ignited World War II in Europe and whose genocidal racial policies led to the Holocaust.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: First Prime Minister of independent India, architect of modern Indian democracy, secularism, and public science, and co-founder of the global Non-Aligned Movement.

name: Agatha Christie
summary: English detective fiction author acclaimed as the 'Queen of Mystery', the best-selling fiction writer of all time, who created iconic sleuths Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple.

name: Vyacheslav Molotov
summary: Old Bolshevik and Stalin's premier diplomatic negotiator who signed the 1939 Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and shaped Soviet post-WWII diplomacy, namesaked in the 'Molotov cocktail'.

name: Josip Broz Tito
summary: Yugoslav communist revolutionary, anti-Nazi Partisan leader, and President who preserved Yugoslav unity and pioneered the Non-Aligned Movement after breaking with Stalin in 1948.

name: Haile Selassie
summary: Emperor of Ethiopia who modernized his nation, defiantly appealed to the League of Nations against fascist Italian invasion, and became a revered figure in Rastafarianism and Pan-Africanism.

name: Bertha Lutz
summary: Brazilian zoologist, politician, and pioneer of the feminist movement in Latin America, who secured women's right to vote in Brazil and fought to enshrine gender equality in the UN Charter.

name: Nikita Khrushchev
summary: Soviet Premier who denounced Stalin's terror in the 'Secret Speech', initiated the cultural Thaw, backed the early Space Race triumphs, and resolved the Cuban Missile Crisis.

name: Plínio Salgado
summary: Writer, journalist, and politician who founded Brazilian Integralism (AIB), leading the largest nationalist-corporatist movement in 1930s Latin America.

name: Jean Piaget
summary: Swiss psychologist renowned for his pioneering work in child development and cognitive developmental psychology, identifying the four stages of childhood mental growth.

name: Lucky Luciano
summary: Italian-American mobster considered the father of modern organized crime in the United States, who established the Five Families of New York and created The Commission.

name: Pixinguinha
summary: Brazilian composer, arranger, flutist, and saxophonist Alfredo da Rocha Viana Filho, considered a foundational pioneer of modern Brazilian popular music and the choro genre.

name: Pope Paul VI
summary: Giovanni Battista Montini, Pope who successfully guided the conclusion and implementation of the Second Vatican Council, fostered ecumenism, and published the landmark encyclical Populorum Progressio.

name: Amelia Earhart
summary: Pioneering American aviation icon and author, the first female aviator to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean, who set numerous records and championed women in aviation.

name: Lampião
summary: Virgulino Ferreira da Silva, the legendary 'Rei do Cangaço' (King of Cangaço), who commanded bandit outlaws across the Brazilian Northeast for nearly two decades.

name: Luís Carlos Prestes
summary: 'The Knight of Hope', military rebel who led the 25,000-km march of the Prestes Column across Brazil, and longtime General Secretary of the Brazilian Communist Party (PCB).

name: Golda Meir
summary: Fourth Prime Minister of Israel ('Iron Lady of Israeli Politics') who co-signed Israel's Declaration of Independence and steered the nation through the 1973 Yom Kippur War.

name: Michał Kalecki
summary: Polish Marxist and macroeconomist who independently developed the core foundations of the principle of effective demand and business cycles before John Maynard Keynes.

name: Alfred Hitchcock
summary: English filmmaker known as the 'Master of Suspense' who pioneered psychological tension, subjective camera techniques, and cinematic editing in cinema history.

name: Al Capone
summary: American gangster and boss of the Chicago Outfit during the Prohibition era, whose criminal empire dominated bootlegging, gambling, and racketeering.

name: Lavrentiy Beria
summary: Chief of the Soviet secret police (NKVD) under Stalin who administered the vast Gulag forced-labor system and ruthlessly directed the Soviet atomic bomb project to completion.

name: Jacques Lacan
summary: French psychoanalyst and psychiatrist who reinterpreted Freud through structural linguistics, famous for the mirror stage and the tripartite order of Real, Symbolic, and Imaginary.

name: Karl Popper
summary: Austrian-British philosopher of science and political philosopher who introduced empirical falsifiability as the criterion of scientific demarcation and defended liberal democracy.

name: Barbara McClintock
summary: American cytogeneticist awarded the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for her groundbreaking discovery of genetic transposition ('jumping genes') in maize.

name: Paul Dirac
summary: English theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate who united quantum mechanics with special relativity through the Dirac Equation, predicting antimatter and the positron.

name: Igor Kurchatov
summary: 'Father of the Soviet atomic bomb', nuclear physicist who directed the Soviet nuclear weapons project (RDS-1) and built the world's first civilian nuclear power plant at Obninsk.

name: Salvador Dalí
summary: Spanish Surrealist painter renowned for his technical virtuosity, dreamlike bizarre imagery, and iconic melting clocks in 'The Persistence of Memory'.

name: B.F. Skinner
summary: American psychologist, behaviorist, and author who pioneered operant conditioning, the Skinner box, and schedules of reinforcement, fundamentally shaping modern behavioral science.

name: Nise da Silveira
summary: Brazilian psychiatrist and Jungian pioneer who revolutionized psychiatric treatment by rejecting aggressive therapies like electroshock and lobotomy in favor of art therapy and humanization.

name: Emmanuel Levinas
summary: Lithuanian-born French phenomenological philosopher who placed ethics as first philosophy, grounded in the immediate and asymmetrical encounter with the Face of the Other.

name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
summary: German Lutheran pastor, theologian, and anti-Nazi dissident who resisted Hitler's totalitarian regime, wrote on 'costly grace', and was executed at Flossenbürg.

name: Leonid Brezhnev
summary: General Secretary who ruled the USSR for 18 years, presiding over military expansion, superpower nuclear parity, the Brezhnev Doctrine, and the era of political stability and economic stagnation.

name: Rachel Carson
summary: American marine biologist and conservationist whose landmark book 'Silent Spring' exposed the environmental hazards of pesticides, sparking the global environmental movement.

name: Sergei Korolev
summary: The anonymous 'Chief Designer' and mastermind of the Soviet space program who launched Sputnik 1, sent Yuri Gagarin into orbit, and inaugurated the human Space Age.

name: Willard Van Orman Quine
summary: American analytic philosopher and logician who dismantled logical positivism with his critiques of the analytic-synthetic distinction and theory of indeterminacy of translation.

name: Cartola
summary: Brazilian singer, composer, and poet Angenor de Oliveira, revered as one of the quintessential figures of samba and co-founder of the legendary Estação Primeira de Mangueira samba school.

name: Simone Weil
summary: French philosopher, mystic, and political activist who gave up academic privilege to work in factories, developing profound philosophies of attention, affliction, and decreation.

name: Ronald Coase
summary: British economist and Nobel laureate who established the foundational theory of transaction costs and property rights, formulating the famous Coase Theorem.

name: Akira Kurosawa
summary: Master Japanese film director and screenwriter whose dynamic visual compositions, humanistic storytelling, and cinematic editing revolutionized world cinema.

name: Chico Xavier
summary: Brazilian spiritual medium, philanthropist, and author who psychographed over 450 books, donating all proceeds to charity and becoming a revered symbol of altruism and peace.

name: Tancredo Neves
summary: Conciliatory statesman and Prime Minister who united the democratic opposition to end 21 years of military rule, elected first civilian President in 1985 before dying on the eve of inauguration.

name: Maria Bonita
summary: Maria Gomes de Oliveira, the 'Rainha do Cangaço' (Queen of Cangaço), the first woman to join Lampião's outlaw band, becoming a legendary figure in Brazilian folklore.

name: Carlos Marighella
summary: Revolutionary Marxist politician, writer, and guerrilla leader who founded the ALN to fight Brazil's military dictatorship and authored the 'Minimanual of the Urban Guerrilla'.

name: Chien-Shiung Wu
summary: Chinese-American experimental physicist known as the 'First Lady of Physics', whose famous Wu Experiment proved that parity is violated in weak nuclear interactions.

name: Luiz Gonzaga
summary: Brazilian singer, songwriter, and accordionist celebrated as the 'King of Baião' (Rei do Baião), who popularized northeastern Brazilian musical genres like baião, xote, and forró nationwide.

name: Pope John Paul I
summary: Albino Luciani, the 'Smiling Pope', whose warm humility and reform-minded 33-day pontificate in 1978 left an indelible imprint on the global Catholic consciousness.

name: Wernher von Braun
summary: Aerospace engineer and architect of modern rocketry, developing the V-2 rocket in Germany and later designing NASA's Saturn V rocket that propelled humans to the Moon.

name: Rosa Parks
summary: American civil rights activist whose courageous refusal to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama in 1955 ignited the Montgomery bus boycott and the modern civil rights movement.

name: Jesse Owens
summary: American track and field athlete who won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympic Games, shattering Adolf Hitler's myth of Aryan racial supremacy on global television.

name: Hedy Lamarr
summary: Austrian-American Hollywood film actress and brilliant inventor who co-invented frequency-hopping spread spectrum technology, the fundamental basis for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS.

name: Jonas Salk
summary: American virologist and medical researcher who developed the first successful inactivated polio vaccine, famously refusing to patent it so it could benefit all humanity.

name: Carlos Lacerda
summary: Journalist, orator, and Governor of Guanabara ('The Crow') whose fiery anti-communist rhetoric and UDN opposition precipitated Vargas's suicide and the 1964 coup.

name: Miguel Arraes
summary: Governor of Pernambuco and leftist icon who empowered rural workers through literacy programs, minimum wage enforcement, and socialist agrarian organizing.

name: Ulysses Guimarães
summary: 'Senhor Diretas' and President of the 1988 Constituent Assembly who mobilized millions for democratic elections and promulgated Brazil's democratic 'Citizen Constitution'.

name: Franco Montoro
summary: Jurist, Governor of São Paulo, and founder of the PSDB who championed administrative decentralization, participatory democracy, and the Diretas Já campaign.

name: Indira Gandhi
summary: First and only female Prime Minister of India, a towering, decisive political leader who navigated the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War and spearheaded the Green Revolution.

name: Jânio Quadros
summary: Populist President of Brazil whose anti-corruption broom campaign, independent foreign policy, and dramatic resignation after seven months plunged the country into crisis.

name: Louis Althusser
summary: French structural Marxist philosopher renowned for his theories of ideology, overdetermination, and Ideological State Apparatuses (ISAs).

name: Katherine Johnson
summary: Legendary American mathematician at NASA whose orbital mechanics calculations were critical to the success of John Glenn's orbit and the Apollo 11 moon landing.

name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
summary: Second President of Egypt, charismatic icon of Pan-Arab nationalism and anti-imperialism who nationalized the Suez Canal and built the Aswan High Dam.

name: João Goulart
summary: 'Jango', reformist President of Brazil whose proposed 'Reformas de Base' (agrarian, educational, and tax reforms) triggered his overthrow in the 1964 military coup.

name: Mikhail Kalashnikov
summary: Legendary Russian small-arms designer who invented the AK-47 assault rifle, celebrated for its rugged mechanical simplicity, reliability, and worldwide military impact.

name: Rosalind Franklin
summary: English chemist and X-ray crystallographer whose famous 'Photo 51' was critical to uncovering the double-helix structure of DNA, alongside pioneering work on viruses and coal.

name: Pope John Paul II
summary: Karol Wojtyła, charismatic Polish pope whose 26-year pontificate helped bring down European Communism, promoted global ecumenism, and traversed 129 countries.

name: Kenneth Arrow
summary: American economist and mathematician who shared the 1972 Nobel Prize, proving Arrow's Impossibility Theorem in social choice and developing General Equilibrium Theory.

name: Andrei Sakharov
summary: Brilliant theoretical physicist and designer of the Soviet thermonuclear bomb who transformed into an outspoken dissident, defender of human rights, and Nobel Peace laureate.

name: Thomas Kuhn
summary: American historian and philosopher of science who coined the terms 'paradigm shift' and 'normal science', arguing that scientific progress proceeds via revolutionary ruptures.

name: Leonel Brizola
summary: Brazilian nationalist politician and governor who launched the Legalidade campaign to defend constitutional democracy in 1961 and pioneered full-time public schools (CIEPs).

name: Paul Feyerabend
summary: Austrian-born philosopher of science renowned for his 'epistemological anarchism', arguing that scientific breakthrough requires methodological freedom ('anything goes').

name: Marlon Brando
summary: American actor widely regarded as the most influential screen actor of the 20th century, revolutionizing acting with raw Stanislavski method realism in 'A Streetcar Named Desire' and 'The Godfather'.

name: Patrice Lumumba
summary: Congolese anti-colonial hero and the first Prime Minister of the independent Democratic Republic of the Congo, whose vision of African self-determination inspired generations.

name: Margaret Thatcher
summary: British statesman known as the 'Iron Lady', Britain's first female prime minister (1979–1990) who reshaped British politics with deregulation, privatization, and decisive Cold War resolve.

name: Miles Davis
summary: American jazz trumpeter, bandleader, and composer who spearheaded nearly every major postwar jazz innovation, including cool jazz, hard bop, modal jazz, and jazz fusion.

name: Marilyn Monroe
summary: American actress, singer, and model who became one of the most enduring cultural icons of the 20th century and a major symbol of Hollywood's golden age.

name: Thich Nhat Hanh
summary: Vietnamese Buddhist monk, peace activist, and author who pioneered 'Engaged Buddhism', global mindfulness practices, and founded Plum Village Monastery in France.

name: Ariano Suassuna
summary: Brazilian playwright, novelist, poet, and philosopher who founded the Movimento Armorial, championing and defending the authentic popular culture of northeastern Brazil.

name: Pope Benedict XVI
summary: Joseph Ratzinger, eminent German theologian and scholar who served as Pope from 2005 until his historic resignation in 2013, championing orthodox doctrine and faith-reason harmony.

name: Stanley Kubrick
summary: American cinematic auteur celebrated for his meticulous technical mastery, groundbreaking visual effects, dark satire, and philosophical inquiries into humanity.

name: Maya Angelou
summary: American memoirist, poet, and civil rights icon whose lyrical autobiographies and inspirational verse celebrate human resilience, dignity, and triumph over oppression.

name: Jürgen Habermas
summary: German Frankfurt School philosopher and sociologist celebrated for his theories of communicative rationality, discursive democracy, and the public sphere.

name: Audrey Hepburn
summary: British actress and humanitarian icon who won an Academy Award for 'Roman Holiday', starred in 'Breakfast at Tiffany's', and dedicated her later life as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

name: Fernanda Montenegro
summary: Acclaimed Brazilian actress widely revered as the 'First Lady of Brazilian Theater', the only Brazilian nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress (Central Station).

name: Neil Armstrong
summary: American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who became the first human to walk on the Moon as commander of Apollo 11 on July 20, 1969.

name: Tu Youyou
summary: Chinese pharmaceutical chemist and malariologist who discovered artemisinin and dihydroartemisinin from sweet wormwood, saving millions of lives and winning the 2015 Nobel Prize.

name: Elza Soares
summary: Legendary Brazilian samba singer acclaimed as BBC's 'Singer of the Millennium', whose gravelly, electric voice became a defiant anthem against racism, poverty, and domestic violence.

name: Mario Covas
summary: Civil engineer, Mayor and Governor of São Paulo, and stalwart of democratic redemocratization known for unwavering ethical integrity, fiscal rigor, and public investments.

name: Itamar Franco
summary: President of Brazil (1992–1995) who restored institutional stability following Collor's impeachment and appointed the economic team that designed and implemented the Plano Real.

name: Thomas Sowell
summary: Economist, social theorist, and Chicago School scholar renowned for empirical critiques of state economic planning, affirmative action, and social engineering.

name: João Gilberto
summary: Brazilian singer, guitarist, and composer hailed as the 'Father of Bossa Nova', who invented the genre's defining syncopated guitar rhythm (violão gago) and whispery vocal delivery.

name: Toni Morrison
summary: Celebrated American novelist, essayist, and editor awarded the 1993 Nobel Prize in Literature for powerful, poetic examinations of the Black American experience and identity.

name: Fernando Henrique Cardoso
summary: 'FHC', internationally renowned sociologist of Dependency Theory and two-term President of Brazil who ended hyperinflation with the Plano Real and modernized state institutions.

name: Andrei Tarkovsky
summary: Russian Soviet filmmaker renowned for his poetic, metaphysical vision, long takes, spiritual inquiry, and philosophical approach to cinema as 'sculpting in time'.

name: Raoni Metuktire
summary: Legendary Brazilian indigenous chief of the Kayapo people, internationally recognized environmental icon with his labret lip plate, and tireless defender of the Amazon.

name: Garrincha
summary: Brazilian football winger renowned as 'A Alegria do Povo' (The Joy of the People), whose mesmerizing dribbling led Brazil to World Cup victories in 1958 and 1962.

name: Yuri Gagarin
summary: Soviet cosmonaut who became the first human in outer space and the first to orbit the Earth on April 12, 1961 aboard Vostok 1.

name: Alexei Leonov
summary: Soviet cosmonaut, Air Force general, and artist who conducted the first spacewalk (extravehicular activity) in human history during the Voskhod 2 mission in 1965.

name: Charles Manson
summary: American cult leader whose apocalyptic commune, the Manson Family, carried out a series of notorious murders in California in 1969 under his psychological manipulation.

name: Jane Goodall
summary: English primatologist and anthropologist renowned for her 60-year study of wild chimpanzees in Gombe Stream National Park, proving that chimpanzees make and use tools.

name: Zilda Arns
summary: Brazilian pediatrician, public health expert, and humanitarian who founded Pastoral da Criança, drastically reducing child mortality across Brazil and Latin America through community health education.

name: Elvis Presley
summary: American singer and actor celebrated as the 'King of Rock and Roll', whose electrifying blend of rhythm & blues and country sparked a musical and youth cultural revolution.

name: Dalai Lama (14th)
summary: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism and 1989 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, revered worldwide for advocating compassion, nonviolence, and Tibetan autonomy.

name: Valentina Tereshkova
summary: Soviet cosmonaut and engineer who became the first woman to fly in space, piloting Vostok 6 on June 16, 1963 and completing 48 orbits of Earth.

name: Bernie Madoff
summary: American financier and former chairman of NASDAQ who orchestrated the largest Ponzi scheme in history, defrauding thousands of investors out of an estimated $64.8 billion.

name: Enéas Carneiro
summary: Cardiologist, mathematician, and founder of PRONA, renowned for fiery 15-second television speeches defending national sovereignty, nuclear deterrence, and state-led industrialism.

name: Jorge Ben Jor
summary: Musical visionary who fused samba, soul, funk, and bossa nova to invent samba-rock, composing foundational global anthems of Afro-Brazilian cultural pride.

name: John Lennon
summary: English singer, songwriter, and peace activist who co-founded The Beatles, forming the most successful songwriting partnership in history with Paul McCartney, and penned 'Imagine'.

name: Al Pacino
summary: Legendary American actor known for explosive emotional intensity and method realism, starring as Michael Corleone in 'The Godfather' trilogy, 'Scarface', and 'Serpico'.

name: Wangari Maathai
summary: Kenyan environmental and political activist who founded the Green Belt Movement and became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize (2004).

name: Bob Dylan
summary: American singer-songwriter and poet who transformed popular music into high literature, receiving the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature 'for having created new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition'.

name: Giorgio Agamben
summary: Italian philosopher whose influential political philosophy investigates the state of exception, biopolitics, and sovereign power over 'bare life' (homo sacer).

name: Jimi Hendrix
summary: American electric guitarist, singer, and songwriter celebrated as the greatest instrumentalist in the history of rock music, revolutionizing guitar tone and sonic feedback.

name: Tim Maia
summary: Larger-than-life Brazilian singer, songwriter, and producer who pioneered soul, funk, and R&B music in Brazil, celebrated for his booming baritone and rebellious charisma.

name: Milton Nascimento
summary: 'Bituca', transcendent Brazilian vocalist and songwriter whose celestial falsetto and Clube da Esquina collective fused jazz, sacred folk, and Afro-Mineiro polyphony.

name: Stephen Hawking
summary: Theoretical physicist and cosmologist who discovered black hole thermal radiation (Hawking Radiation) and popularized cosmological inquiry through 'A Brief History of Time'.

name: Bobby Fischer
summary: American chess prodigy and 11th World Chess Champion who broke the Soviet monopoly on chess by defeating Boris Spassky in the legendary 1972 'Match of the Century'.

name: Robert De Niro
summary: American actor and producer acclaimed for transformative psychological immersion in collaborations with Martin Scorsese, including 'Taxi Driver', 'Raging Bull', and 'Goodfellas'.

name: Lech Wałęsa
summary: Polish shipyard electrician and trade unionist who co-founded Solidarity (Solidarność), spearheading the peaceful collapse of Soviet-backed communism in Eastern Europe.

name: Vint Cerf
summary: 'Father of the Internet', Turing Award laureate who co-designed the TCP/IP protocols and the basic fundamental architecture of the global Internet.

name: Maria da Penha
summary: Brazilian biopharmacist and women's rights leader whose survival of domestic violence and landmark legal battle at the OAS resulted in Brazil's historic Maria da Penha Law.

name: Elis Regina
summary: Legendary Brazilian singer widely celebrated as the greatest female vocalist in the history of MPB (Música Popular Brasileira), known for dramatic vocal mastery and emotional intensity.

name: Raul Seixas
summary: Iconic Brazilian singer-songwriter, mystic, and countercultural pioneer celebrated as the 'Father of Brazilian Rock', who blended American rock'n'roll with northeastern baião rhythms.

name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
summary: Metallurgical labor leader during the ABC strikes, co-founder of the Workers' Party (PT), and three-time President of Brazil recognized for pioneering anti-poverty programs.

name: Ted Bundy
summary: Infamous American serial killer, kidnapper, and necrophile who murdered at least 30 young women across multiple states during the 1970s while using charismatic deception.

name: Freddie Mercury
summary: British singer, songwriter, and flamboyant frontman of rock band Queen, revered for his phenomenal four-octave vocal range, theatrical songwriting, and legendary Live Aid performance.

name: David Bowie
summary: English singer-songwriter, actor, and musical chameleon whose theatrical reinventions (Ziggy Stardust, Thin White Duke) transformed rock, glam, electronic, and pop culture.

name: Sally Ride
summary: American physicist and astronaut who became the first American woman and third woman in space aboard Space Shuttle Challenger (STS-7) in 1983.

name: Robin Williams
summary: Beloved American actor and comedian renowned for his rapid-fire improvisational genius, emotional range, and iconic roles across comedy and profound drama.

name: Benazir Bhutto
summary: Pakistani democratic politician who became the first woman to head a democratic government in a Muslim-majority nation, serving twice as Prime Minister of Pakistan.

name: El Chapo (Joaquín Guzmán)
summary: Mexican drug lord who headed the Sinaloa Cartel, orchestrating transnational trafficking through elaborate border tunnels and staging two sensational prison escapes.

name: Jeffrey Dahmer
summary: American serial killer and sex offender known as the 'Milwaukee Cannibal', who murdered and dismembered 17 men and boys between 1978 and 1991.
